test_title: PYST 53: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 08 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A bus travelling at 28 km/hr completes a journey in 20 hours. What should its speed be to cover the same distance in 14 hours?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time.

Time ratio = 20 : 14 = 10 : 7

Speed ratio = 7 : 10

Given, 7 units = 28 km/hr ⇒ 1 unit = 4 km/hr

Required speed (10 units) = 10 × 4 = 40 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial speed (S₁) = 28 km/hr

Initial time (T₁) = 20 hours

New time (T₂) = 14 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

 Distance is Constant
 
• 
 
 
 
 Distance (D)
 S1 = 28 km/hr | T1 = 20 hours
 
• 
 
 
 
 Same Distance (D)
 S2 = ? km/hr | T2 = 14 hours
 S1 × T1 = S2 × T2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in the first case = S₁ × T₁

⇒ Distance = 28 × 20 = 560 km

⇒ Since the distance remains the same, for the second case:

⇒ S₂ × T₂ = 560

⇒ S₂ × 14 = 560

⇒ S₂ = 560 ÷ 14

⇒ S₂ = 40 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 40 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion

When Distance is constant, Speed and Time are inversely proportional. Thus, S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂.

Average Speed

When traveling two equal halves of a distance at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
